Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 5-day history of dry cough (every 20–30 min), continuous green rhinorrhoea, subjective fever/chills, myalgias  
• No dyspnoea, chest pain, haemoptysis, or sore throat; brief self-limited diarrhoea at onset  
• PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension; meds as above  
• No current vitals or physical exam available (telehealth)  

Working diagnosis  
• Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness – most consistent with symptom pattern, time course, and absence of red-flag features.  

Considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript)  
• COVID-19 infection – medium likelihood given overlap of symptoms; recommend testing per local guidelines.  
• Post-viral or early acute bacterial sinusitis – medium likelihood due to green nasal discharge >5 days; monitor for worsening facial pain, persistent fever.  

Management  
• Symptomatic care: continue Lemsip (caution about total daily paracetamol dose); maintain hydration.  
• Temperature monitoring: purchase thermometer; track readings.  
• Safety-net advice: seek review if temperature ≥ 37.5-38 °C persists, cough worsens, purulent or bloody sputum develops, dyspnoea, chest pain, or new systemic deterioration.  
• Chronic disease follow-up: ensure routine diabetes (HbA1c, renal profile) and blood pressure checks with GP.  
• No antibiotics indicated at present; consider if bacterial superinfection suspected on review.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness – High likelihood: classic presentation with dry cough, rhinorrhoea, myalgias, subjective fever of 5 days.  
2. COVID-19 infection – Medium likelihood: contemporary prevalence and similar symptom complex; lacks anosmia/dyspnoea but remains plausible.  
3. Acute bacterial sinusitis (post-viral) – Medium likelihood: green nasal discharge >5 days; monitor for escalating sinus pain or persistent fever.
